_note: Catalog cross-checked against the AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022): the mandatory Common Criteria CC1-CC9 enumerate 33 individual criteria (CC1:5, CC2:3, CC3:4, CC4:2, CC5:3, CC6:8, CC7:5, CC8:1, CC9:2), plus the four optional categories added in scope by choice — Availability (3), Confidentiality (2), Processing Integrity (5), Privacy (18). ADR-069's draft said 32; corrected to 33 against the authoritative enumeration (ADR-069 change log, 2026-06-24). Each term carries its category and an `optional` flag (false for CC, true for the four optional categories — in-scope-by-choice). Paperwork existence/metadata/freshness only; ctxgrd never attests that a control operated over the period — operating-effectiveness adequacy is the auditor's judgment (ADR-069 Context).
summary: SOC 2 control-to-evidence register (SOC2) over the security base — AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, rev. 2022): the mandatory Common Criteria CC1-CC9 plus the optional Availability/Confidentiality/Processing-Integrity/Privacy categories. Paperwork existence/metadata/freshness only, never operating-effectiveness adequacy.

namespaces.name: SOC2
namespaces.comment: SOC 2 control-to-evidence register (AICPA Trust Services Criteria, SOC-001/002/003). Each entry maps one Trust Services criterion (from the closed catalog, projected into core.allowed-values) to its implementing control and operating-effectiveness evidence — a reused POLICY, an ADR, or an `evidence_link` (an access-review log, change ticket, or config export). SOC 2 introduces no statutory document namespace of its own; the criterion-to-control-to-evidence mapping is its sole artifact, reusing POLICY/RISK/VULN from the security base. Path-claim with an `id` so an audit or a cross-ref can resolve a control. core.calendar-freshness over `reviewed_date` surfaces a stale control (the Type I / Type II distinction lives at the freshness layer: a stale review is a point-in-time snapshot masquerading as period evidence). soc2.control-evidence (SOC-002) reuses the hipaa.safeguard-evidence conditional machinery: an in-scope control asserting a criterion with neither a POLICY/ADR cross-ref nor a non-empty `evidence_link` fails; a `not-applicable` control is out of scope. The `status` vocabulary is deliberately open (ADR-114 § STV-001) — a program's lifecycle words are its own — with one machine-read exception: the `out-of-scope-status` value must be spelled `not-applicable` (case-insensitive), or the Statement-of-Applicability exemption does not apply and the control is held to the evidence requirement. The freshness field is `reviewed_date`, one spelling across this whole family (ADR-114 § FLD-001): it records when the review happened, which is what core.calendar-freshness ages.
